_comment: The branch protection this repository's main branch is MISSING, written down
exactly, so that applying it is a mechanical step rather than a judgement call.
Round-3 finding P1-13: live metadata shows main has no required status checks,
no required pull request reviews and no rulesets. Draft status on a pull request
is not branch protection — it stops a merge button, not a push.
THIS FILE IS NOT APPLIED BY ANYTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY, AND MUST NOT BE.
Writing branch protection is a control-plane mutation on the GitHub repository:
it needs an administrative token, it changes who can merge what, and it is
outside the authorization this code round has. It is recorded here, and the
TASKBOARD row that tracks it stays unfinished, until an operator with that
authorization applies it deliberately. tests/release/branch-protection-contract.test.mjs
asserts that no script in the repository writes it.
Why the contexts are job names and not 'workflow / job': for GitHub Actions the
check run that a protection rule matches is created per job and named with the
job's `name:`, so 'Repository validation' is the context. A context that does
not correspond to a job which actually runs on a pull_request event blocks every
pull request forever — which is why `required_status_checks.contexts` below is
restricted to the pull_request-reachable jobs and is verified against
.github/workflows/ci.yml by the contract test.
Relationship to infra/release/required-jobs.json: that manifest is what
infra/systemd/newme-deploy.sh requires of a release-final workflow_dispatch run
on main BEFORE it will deploy. This file is what GitHub must require of a pull
request BEFORE it can reach main. The deploy manifest is therefore a superset:
it additionally names 'Release-final taskboard completion', which is
dispatch-only by design and can never run on a pull request. Putting that job
in the contexts below would deadlock every pull request; leaving it out of the
deploy manifest would let an incomplete taskboard reach production. Both
directions are asserted by the contract test.
authorization: requires a repository-admin token; not granted to this code round

why: It is a single `run: echo ok` step. It runs on every pull request and every
push to main and it is always green, because there is nothing in it that can
fail. Requiring it would add a context that proves the runner started and
nothing else, and reading it as CI evidence is the specific mistake the
review calls out. It is left in place because the F-04 workflow-YAML gate
tracks it, and it is named here so that 'why is this check not required'
has a written answer instead of being an oversight.
so it cannot run for a pull request and would block every merge if required.
It is required at the other boundary instead — infra/release/required-jobs.json,
checked by the deploy wrapper against the release-final run it is handed.
